guarantees.claim: When mux_sel_buf_kmac is not SelApp, SelOutLen, or SelSw (including SelNone), kmac_valid_o=0, kmac_data_o=0, kmac_mask_o=0, app_data_ready=0, and sw_ready_o=1.
In SelApp mode, kmac_valid_o = app_i[app_id].valid, kmac_data_o = app_i[app_id].data, kmac_mask_o byte lanes are all-1 for each set bit in app_i[app_id].strb, and app_data_ready = kmac_ready_i.
In SelOutLen mode, kmac_valid_o is always 1, kmac_data_o = MsgWidth'(encoded_outlen), kmac_mask_o = MsgWidth'(encoded_outlen_mask).
In SelSw mode, kmac_valid_o = sw_valid_i, kmac_data_o = sw_data_i, kmac_mask_o = sw_mask_i, and sw_ready_o = kmac_ready_i.
In SelApp, each group of 8 bits of kmac_mask_o starting at bit 8*i is set to 8'hFF if app_i[app_id].strb[i] is 1, else 8'h00.
sw_ready_o is held at 1 when mux_sel_buf_kmac is not SelSw, including SelApp and SelOutLen cases.

assumptions.claim: mux_sel_buf_kmac must be one-hot, i.e., exactly one of SelApp, SelOutLen, SelSw active at a time.
assumptions.risk: Multiple active select bits may cause simulation-synthesis mismatch, output glitches, or unintended data transmission.

assumptions.claim: app_id must be a legal index into the app_i array.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds read returns X or garbage, potentially leaking secret/corrupt data into kmac_data_o/kmac_mask_o.

uncertain_points.claim: app_id is used directly to index app_i without range checking; an invalid app_id can read out-of-bounds data into the KMAC output path.
uncertain_points.cond: When mux_sel_buf_kmac selects SelApp and app_id is out of range.
uncertain_points.risk: Secret or random memory contents may be written to kmac_data_o/mask_o, bypassing data origin security.

uncertain_points.claim: encoded_outlen is cast to MsgWidth'(encoded_outlen); if encoded_outlen bit-width exceeds MsgWidth, high-order bits are truncated.
uncertain_points.cond: When mux_sel_buf_kmac == SelOutLen and encoded_outlen width > MsgWidth.
uncertain_points.risk: Output length specifier may be incorrect, leading to wrong digest length or protocol error.

uncertain_points.claim: kmac_mask_o byte-expansion loop writes to kmac_mask_o[8*i+:8]; if MsgWidth (the width of kmac_mask_o) is less than 8*$bits(strb), the assignment writes beyond the signal width.
uncertain_points.risk: Out-of-bounds write truncates high bytes of mask, possibly unmasking bytes that should have been masked, leading to data corruption or security bypass.
